findings.summary: The delta introduces a format-gate failure. Running `prettier --check` on the current tree flags DESIGN-DECISIONS.md and docs/meta/adr/README.md. The new ADR-0057 rows are not padded to the table's column widths, and the edited ADR-0055/0056 rows widen the last column. The HEAD copies of both files pass Prettier, and every other changed file passes. The recorded format check covered only the four policy/config/test files, so it did not catch this.
findings.failure_scenario: The repository `format:check` step (`prettier --check .`, which the CI foundation format gate runs, and which is the first step of `pnpm check`) fails on the candidate. This blocks the required-green PR. Fix it by formatting those two tables only (prettier --write on the two files), then rerun format:check across the whole repository. No content change is needed. Docs that claim 'law/format checks passed' should keep that claim scoped to the four files that were actually checked.

findings.summary: The front-matter `supersedes: ['ADR-0055','ADR-0056']` is an unqualified machine-readable field. The body text and both index rows limit the supersession to activation timing and keep 0055/0056 Accepted.
findings.failure_scenario: Any docs-governance or ADR-index tooling that reads `supersedes` could treat ADR-0055 and ADR-0056 as fully superseded, even though their source obligations remain binding. Doctor docs-governance passed on this tree, so nothing breaks today. Consider recording the partial scope in a structured field, or confirm that the existing convention accepts partial supersedes.
